## Retracting my previous comment — and this ticket appears ALREADY FIXED on `origin/main`

**Retraction first.** My previous comment claimed a within-file drift: that `transition.txt`'s
usage line omitted `--ref` while the body documented it. **That is wrong — no such
inconsistency exists.** I was reading the pre-RP-05 file in a checkout pinned at `8fa8f36b64`,
where `transition.txt` is 11 lines of hand-written prose. On `origin/main` the file is a
22-line generated artifact. I compared a stale tree against a claim about the current one.

**But the diagnosis matters more than the retraction, because the current file is not what this
ticket describes either.** At `origin/main`, `src/rebar/_cli/help/transition.txt` **documents
`--caused-by`** — in the usage block (line 2, `[--class CLOSE_CLASS] [--caused-by CAUSED_BY]`)
and in the options body (lines 19-20, "ticket that caused this bug"). Reproduce with:

```
git show origin/main:src/rebar/_cli/help/transition.txt | grep -n caused
```

which returns three hits. The two-source drift this ticket was filed for is gone.

### What closed it, and why the timing hid it

`22efd71f10` "RP-05 S2d: generate CLI help from factories" (Thu 2026-08-20 20:23:30 -0700,
merged; `git merge-base --is-ancestor` confirms). This ticket was created 2026-08-20 17:00:02 —
**about 3.4 hours before that landed.** So it was valid when filed and was overtaken by
in-flight work, which is exactly the case that is easy to miss.

RP-05 S2d did not patch the wording. It removed the second source: `scripts/gen_cli_help.py`
(new, 200 lines) renders `help/*.txt` **from the parser factories**, so `build_transition` is now
the single authority and a flag cannot be registered without appearing in the help.

### The remedy this ticket proposed is already implemented, with teeth

`gen_cli_help.py --check` "fails on any missing / stale / stray artifact", and
`tests/unit/test_gen_cli_help.py` exercises it — `test_check_mode_passes_on_committed_artifacts`
asserts the committed bytes are current, and `test_check_detects_a_stale_artifact`,
`_a_missing_artifact`, and `_a_stray_artifact` mutation-check that `--check` actually fails when
it should. That is the "test asserting every parser-registered flag appears in the help" idea,
implemented structurally (generation) rather than as an assertion over a hand-maintained file.

Worth noting for `project.portability`: the gate rides in the **unit suite**, not in `make lint`
and not as a CI-only step, so it triggers in any environment that runs the tests.

### Recommendation

Re-verify against `origin/main` and, if this holds, close as **`obsolete`** (the premise no
longer holds — the second source is gone) rather than `superseded`, unless the RP-05 story is
preferred as a named replacement link. Not closing it myself: not my ticket and not my lane.

**One correction to the note above mine.** It states `--caused-by` is "absent from that file
entirely — from both the usage and the body". That is accurate for the *old* 11-line file, but
not for the 22-line `origin/main` artifact it quotes: the quoted excerpt skips line 2 and lines
19-20, which are the `--caused-by` entries. Flagging it only so a future implementer does not
conclude the file changed under them.

Evidence gathered while closing `1e48-ff69-13f7-4a83`.
